author: Zintenka
body:
I've heard on the OCN post that Badlion wouldn't be willing to merge with them, I've also heard the exact opposite and I've also heard that their 50/50 on it.

I feel that OCN merging with Badlion would not be a good idea because from what I'm hearing, Badlion wouldn't know what to do with OCN and would just let it rot.

Revised to suit the better conditions I suggested for my reply to Para:

I'm aware of the probable worth that OCN has (Which is why they're shutting down anyway)

We could use their source code to possibly enhance Avicus and be allowed to use their maps for our server.

Perhaps only merging with OCN in spirit and through them handing over their assets. Rather than officially, I wager that the reason that OCN costs so much is probably because of beastnode and how many servers they use.

They over-complicated it so much that it worked against them. Acquiring their assets that they developed themselves costs nil.

Plus, acquiring a few more developers on Avicus as well as merging the staff teams together would work out for everyone.

Avicus would still be left as Avicus, just that things would be developed with faster and greater efficiency, we'd have a lot more maps, a lot more players.

Avicus regulars would still call Avicus home, and OCN regulars can move to a home away from home.

What are your thoughts on this?

Common sense applies here, so don't be a smart-ass.

This is a serious and open discussion, let's keep it that way.

replies.author: gobernment
replies.body:
We are not going to acquire OCN. We already have the plugins we need, and Atlas will contain a lot of things Overcast may have and possibly more. Also, we didn't convert to XML because OCN did it. We used to use XML back in MCZone and it was more professional compared to YML which looks like a shopping list.

OCN would not give us anything we don't already have. We would probably also get into debt if we tried merging/purchasing (I want to bet it's a steep price, 4 years of development), and most OCN regulars already know about Avicus.

It is NOT a good business idea.

replies.author: Zintenka
replies.body:
I re-evaluated everything I said with OCN merging with Avicus when I made the response to Para because I realized the flaws to it...

I mean we merge with OCN's spirit. We keep our brand, we keep our name but we just acquire OCN's staff team, maps, source code to tweak how we please and add to our own.

It'd be like Kohi and Badlion, Kohi no longer exists but Badlion ate it.

We "eat" OCN and keep all their assets, however we dump what caused OCN to be so expensive in the first place.

I'm pretty sure maps, staff and the source code weren't part of the problem since those aren't done with contracts and stuff....

Anyway, if a player is banned on OCN but not banned on Avicus since we're still Avicus those banned on OCN will still be welcome here... just if they get banned again... it'd be like someone being banned on Avicus normally.

Those banned on Avicus will stay banned until appealed.

We keep our rules since this is Avicus. It's up to Funky to decide what rules of OCN we could possibly add and replace to enhance Avicus.

As for the mod team of OCN, they're human. They can adapt to Avicus' way of doing things, if they can't they can just be normal players.

replies.author: ALM
replies.body:
Our infrastructure and backend are extremely incompatible with the way OCN does things. We use two totally different database structures, so much of their code would be extremely hard to incorporate. The only real thing we could benefit from is their 1.9 fixes and some of their open-source projects on Github. Us using their PGM code/XML syntax would be impractical at best, as we have already developed an XML structure for Atlas. We would be open to adding features that are available in PGM, if highly requested.

You can see what is available in Atlas here.

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
If we combined staff, it'll become a huge mess.

Moderation on the Overcast Network and the Avicus Network is extremely different.
Although I haven't been staff on OCN, I'm aware of the differences and how the staff there work. There'll be a LOT of clashes and it just won't work.

Former Avcius Moderator and current Overcast Moderator/Event Co-ordinator Lieutenantpants left Avicus because they disagreed a lot. If we had the OCN dev and mod team, it'll be this, but on a much bigger scale, which will be disastrous for Avicus. 

By all means, I would love for OCN players to come over and check out this server and having OCN maps would be awesome but I don't think we're allowed to do that legally. 

Making Avicus a place for Overcast players to play is a great idea, but I think in the interests of both servers, we should stop at that.

The Nile: People would not dig, as digging isn't a popular defense trick on this server. What I mean is I Don't want OCN code to be on the server or any games related to the server on the network, unless Avicus has a good twist on it.

If they were to even merge we'd get the players, Hurrary! But I really don't think its necessary to have their Destroy & Capture codes on Avicus and besides that'd mean another Huge update (for the code) and a long wait.

I like the idea of us getting OCN players on the network, but I dislike the idea of having their code on Avicus.
We all want Avicus not OCN 2.

replies.author: DonaldMyTrump
replies.body:
I talked to funky about this momentarily after ocn's closing was announced. Here are a few takeaways:
-Avicus has no interest in OCN plugins
-OCN staff are free to apply here as individuals
-OCN map makers would have to give their maps to avicus individually, in order to buy out OCN they would expect money, most likely well above their worth.
